claim: Respondents determined by the commission in G. L. c. 151B § 5 proceedings to have committed discriminatory acts in employment are entitled only to administrative review under G. L. c. 30A, and do not possess a State constitutional right to a jury trial, thereby overruling the contrary holding in Lavelle.
initial_reasoning: The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court decision reported at 441 Mass. 549 held that parties found by the commission in G.L.c. 151B §5 proceedings are limited to administrative review under G.L.c. 30A and do not have a constitutional right to a jury trial, expressly overruling the earlier Lavelle decision. This directly affirms the claim.
